title: eval-harness: per-prompt CI metrics hook + quality gating for prompt-set regressions
author: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Adds a per-prompt CI metrics hook to the eval-harness and a quality gating rule that fails CI when prompt-set regressions exceed configurable thresholds. Motivation: teams have been seeing intermittent model regressions that only surface for specific prompts; existing gate checks at the dataset level miss per-prompt degradations. This PR implements a lightweight hook that runs per-prompt metrics (accuracy, hallucination-rate proxy, token-termination rate) and aggregates to both per-prompt and prompt-set alerts.

What I changed: 1) new eval hook implementation under eval-harness/ci/hooks/per_prompt_metrics_hook.py (callable from existing CI runner) 2) a new gating rule config schema (eval-harness/config/gating/per_prompt_gates.yaml) with thresholds and aggregation strategies 3) integration into the GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/eval-ci.yml) to run the hook in PR checks and upload a summarized JSON artifact 4) unit and integration tests (tests/ci/test_per_prompt_hook.py, tests/evals/test_thresholding.py) 5) docs and examples (docs/eval-harness/per-prompt-gating.md)

Checklist: - [x] Implementation + unit tests - [x] Integration into CI workflow - [x] Documentation and examples - [x] Linear ticket linked - [x] Verified gating behavior locally and in staging

Design notes: - Per-prompt checks are intentionally configurable; by default we run fast proxy metrics (generation length, stop-token frequency, model confidence from logit probing) to keep CI runtime under the existing budget. - The hook emits both a human-friendly summary and a machine-readable JSON artifact that can be consumed by downstream automation (rollbacks, notif). - To avoid noisy failures, gates support a rolling-window and minimum-sample-size; the default gating policy requires at least 20 samples per prompt.

Related work: ENG-9421 adds upstream eval metric collectors; this PR depends on the sampling improvements from ENG-10412.

Commits: squash: implement per-prompt metrics hook; add gating schema; add tests; update CI workflow; docs.

Files changed (high level): - eval-harness/ci/hooks/per_prompt_metrics_hook.py (new) - eval-harness/config/gating/per_prompt_gates.yaml (new) - .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml (modified) - tests/ci/test_per_prompt_hook.py (new) - tests/evals/test_thresholding.py (new) - docs/eval-harness/per-prompt-gating.md (new) - eval-harness/ci/reporting/formatters.py (small adjustments)

Testing: - Local unit tests: all pass. - Staging run against the main prompt-set: simulated regression introduced and gate tripped as expected; artifact uploaded. - Performance: hook runs in ~6 minutes against 300 prompt-sample partition (within CI budget).

CI notes: there was an initial failure in the e2e eval job due to a flaky sampling helper; I pushed a fix in the same branch (commit 3) to add a deterministic fallback. The e2e job was re-run and passed.
commits: 3 commits: (1) add per_prompt_metrics_hook implementation and schema; (2) tests + docs; (3) fix flaky sampling helper and CI workflow adjustments
review_comments:
Ben Hughes (reviewer): Can we make the default gating policy conservative (higher sample min) to avoid noisy failures for low-traffic prompts?
Author (Asha): Yes — default min_sample_size is 20 and is documented; added config comments to make it easy to override per-repo.
Maya Chen (reviewer): Looks good but please add a short note on expected CI runtime to docs so teams can opt-in if they're sensitive to CI minutes.
Author (Asha): Added runtime estimate in docs and added a CI flag to opt-out.
Ravi Srinivasan (approver): Approved after nits fixed. CI flaky sampling issue identified and fixed in follow-up commit.
release_notes:
- Added per-prompt CI metrics hook (eval-harness)
- New configurable per-prompt gating schema with sensible defaults
- CI workflow integration: per-prompt checks run on PR and upload artifacts
- Docs: guidelines for teams to opt into per-prompt gating and runtime expectations
